subject.title: fix(discord): disable ws 8.21.0 receiver part limits for gateway sockets

question: Should OpenClaw disable ws retained-part receiver limits for Discord gateway sockets while relying on the existing 16 MiB `maxPayload` cap and trusted Discord gateway peer boundary?
rationale: The code path is narrow and dependency behavior matches the proposed options, but the PR overrides a dependency security hardening default on an external network socket.

options.title: Accept Discord-scoped disablement
options.body: Land the PR if maintainers agree the Discord gateway peer is trusted enough and `maxPayload` is the intended remaining resource boundary.

options.title: Require finite retained-part caps
options.body: Ask the contributor to choose high explicit `maxBufferedChunks` and `maxFragments` values with proof that they cover observed Discord traffic.

options.title: Choose another mitigation
options.body: Pause or reject this branch in favor of a ws downgrade, upstream fix, or alternate gateway transport approach.

recommendation.title: Accept Discord-scoped disablement
recommendation.body: Land the PR if maintainers agree the Discord gateway peer is trusted enough and `maxPayload` is the intended remaining resource boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history on Discord gateway transport behavior and diagnostics around this exact failure mode.
